en.title: 7 Essential First Steps in Grand Theft Auto VI
en.summary: Dive into GTA VI with these crucial early-game actions to maximize your experience in Leonida from the moment you gain control.
en.body:
## 1. Explore Your Immediate Surroundings
Before you even think about hitting the open road, take a moment to explore Jason's home. Beyond the now-memed house preparations, you can find small stat boosts from workout equipment and books, and even interact with his pet snake for a focus buff. This early exploration shows Rockstar's dedication to detail, allowing players to absorb the atmosphere and find minor advantages before the chaos truly begins.

## 2. Secure Your Hard-Earned Cash
Losing your money to the police or a sticky end is a brutal early-game setback. Utilize ATMs to stash your cash safely; it's your lifeline for essential weapons, upgrades, and mission progression in the sprawling state of Leonida. This simple act of financial prudence can save you hours of grinding later.

## 3. Repair Your Safehouse
Your starting safehouse is more than just a place to rest; it's a crucial hub that needs attention. Completing repairs not only makes it more functional but also signifies your commitment to establishing a base of operations. This is a foundational step that unlocks further opportunities within the game world.

## 4. Get Lucia Some New Threads
While the focus is often on Jason, remember Lucia is a key part of the narrative. Helping her out by getting new clothes from Andy is a great way to engage with her character arc early on and unlock unique dialogue or interactions. It’s a small gesture that enriches the storytelling.

## 5. Master the Art of Evasion
Understanding how the wanted system works is paramount in any Grand Theft Auto game, and GTA VI is no exception. Provoke the cops in controlled bursts to learn how to escape, hotwire cars, and utilize the environment to your advantage. Becoming proficient in these early chases will make surviving the bigger messes much easier.

## 6. Investigate Shirley's Rum
This early side mission offers a glimpse into the more unconventional tasks awaiting you. Engaging with "Shirley's Rum" provides a taste of the diverse activities beyond the main story and can lead to unexpected rewards. It’s a perfect example of the rich side content Rockstar Games is known for.

## 7. Loot the Crashed Plane
Discovering and looting the crashed plane is a prime example of the emergent gameplay and hidden treasures within Leonida. This event provides valuable resources and a sense of discovery, rewarding players who venture off the beaten path. It’s a thrilling early-game find that can give you a significant advantage.

content_raw: After years of anticipation, rumors, leaks, and delays, Grand Theft Auto VI is finally available. And by almost every account, it lives up to the hype. The game is currently sitting at a near-perfect score of 99 on Metacritic , with professional reviewers, streamers, and regular gamers alike lauding the game for its outlandish attention to detail, mission variety, and jaw dropping graphics. Even if you’ve already managed to put a couple dozen hours into GTA VI , it’s clear that this is a massive game, both in terms of the single player story and the enormous state of Leonida you’re free to explore. These are just a few tips to get started. Warning: some minor spoilers follow. Take a Look Around Your House GTA VI opens with a couple lengthy, unskippable missions. It will be around 30-40 minutes before you can actually start to explore the world, and while it may be tempting to steal the first car you see and head to Vice City, there’s actually quite a bit to do just around Jason’s house. The internet has already made memes about the painting and shingling to be done to prepare for Lucia’s release from prison , but there are also some books around the house and workout equipment to check out for small stat bonuses early on. You can also watch some hilarious stuff on TV, shoot hoops, check out the neighborhood on a bike, and explore the nearby waters in a kayak. Oh, and don’t forget that even feeding Jason’s pet snake once a day boosts your focus. You can easily kill a few hours barely leaving the immediate neighborhood. Stash Your Cash At the start of the game, Jason either keeps cash on him, or hidden in his bedroom. The thing is, if you get arrested or killed, you lose all that cash you’re carrying. That can be a minor annoyance if you’re holding onto a few hundred dollars, or a major set back if you lose a few grand. Cash is king in GTA VI . You’ll need it for various missions, weapons, upgrades, and cosmetics. Eventually, you’ll need a good chunk just to move forward with the story. So, be smart and regularly deposit money you don’t immediately need at home. Get Used to the New Controls Ever since the Grand Theft Auto series moved to the third dimension with 2001’s GTA III , the mapping of controls hasn’t changed much, even through GTA V . While the actions you’ll perform in GTA VI are pretty much the same as they’ve always been, Rockstar has remapped almost everything. Most notably, sprinting is now controlled by clicking the left stick on either PlayStation 5 or the Xbox Series. Jumping and climbing move to the X and A buttons on their respective consoles, and those buttons also now control handbraking in vehicles. The new controls actually feel pretty natural, and given the slower pace of most missions in the opening hours it’s a pretty smooth adjustment, but you’re also free to customize controls in the settings if you want an experience closer to the previous GTA games.
